websearch.worst: A: summary says published version found no effect on lines of code, omitting the log-transformed result favoring treatment (P=0.0103)
websearch.worst_summary_quote: It also found no difference in promotions and no effect on lines of code for engineers.
websearch.worst_page_quote: When using log 2 (1 + code lines) the difference has a P value of 0.0103, with treatment having the higher average values.
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader may think the published trial's code-output data were uniformly null, when one transformation showed a significant positive treatment difference.
websearch.notes: Usable pages: PMC11208135 (primary), breeze.pm, nber w30292 (5011 chars), IGL (2007 chars, abstract only). The 8% lines-of-code claim from the 2022 NBER draft is in no fetched page (C, maybe from unfetched conference.nber.org PDF). Other numbers (1,612; one-third; 13%; 22% with choice not randomized; 12%->8% selection) are supported.

webfetch.fetch_prompt: Find what the randomized studies in this article report about the effect of remote or hybrid work on productivity. Summarize each randomized study's design, sample, and productivity findings, and note any null or negative results and the authors' stated limitations.
webfetch.notes: Spot-checked design, sample, managers -2.6% to +1.0%, take-up 55%/40%, 653 engineers, P=0.0103 note; all match page. No truncation noted.
